newsitem.title: BELGIUM: Confidence jumped in Europe last month.
newsitem.headline: Confidence jumped in Europe last month.

text.p: Confidence among European businesses and consumers rose in February, reflecting strength in construction and better employment prospects, the European Union's executive body said Monday.
The European Commission said its index of economic sentiment jumped to 101.1 in February from 100.3 in January, reflecting improvement in all areas. The index averaged 98.9 for all of 1996.
Among the areas with the biggest gains was the construction industry, where upbeat employment expectations brought the reading to the highest level since December 1995.
In Germany, while the overall reading rose for the fifth consecutive month, consumer confidence worsened due to growing worries over personal finances and a sluggish economy.
Germany has been struggling with record unemployment, which most likely has contributed to the more gloomy assessment by consumers, officials said.
Another factor contributing to the February rise in EU sentiment was the ongoing increase in stock prices.
While the weight of share prices in the EU index is only one sixth, the sharp rise in European markets since the beginning of the year has nonetheless had a positive influence on sentiment.
